title: Low-Level Environmental Lead Exposure and Children's Intellectual Function: An International Pooled Analysis
quick: Lead can harm children's developing brains, even at relatively low blood levels.
details: Estimated IQ decrements 3.9,1.9,1.1 points across 2.4–10,10–20,20–30 mcg/dL respectively; nonlinear model.
funding: Exact primary grant list not extracted
financial_ties: No competing financial interests per indexed publisher text
verification: Indexed primary abstract and publisher disclosure
limitations: Observational estimates, not individual predictions or safe thresholds; do not use IQ chart to diagnose.

title: Risk Factors and Pregnancy
quick: Lead stored in bones can enter the blood during pregnancy.
details: Review exposure sources with clinician; renovation, water, imported products, occupation, pica and take-home exposures matter.
limitations: No autonomous testing or treatment thresholds.

title: Preventing Childhood Lead Poisoning
quick: No safe blood lead level has been identified.
details: Reduce dust/paint, contaminated soil/water, products and take-home exposures; screening with clinician.
limitations: Reference value not a toxicity threshold; prior PED-LEAD related, not independent trial.

title: Lead and Breastfeeding
quick: Lead exposure requires individualized feeding and clinical assessment.
details: Blood lead can be transferred; current clinical guidance specific to level and infant follow-up.
limitations: No automatic breastfeeding cessation or threshold decision engine.

title: Basic Information about Lead in Drinking Water
quick: Use cold tap water for cooking/drinking, and a properly certified filter if lead is a concern.
details: Lead can enter water via plumbing. Boiling does not remove lead; verify contaminant-specific certification.
limitations: Local testing and instructions determine safe source; no universal flush duration.

title: Advice about Eating Fish
quick: Choose lower-mercury fish, rather than avoiding all seafood.
details: US guidance 8–12 oz/week lower-mercury seafood for pregnancy/lactation; age-specific portions for children; local catch advisories.
limitations: Prior P5-29 link; not a new study or universal prescription.

title: Prenatal exposure to organophosphate pesticides and IQ in 7-year-old children
quick: Higher prenatal exposure was linked to lower scores at age seven.
details: Highest vs lowest maternal urinary DAP quintile 7.0 IQ points lower; adjusted for maternal IQ/education, home environment and assessment language.
funding: EPA, NIEHS P01 ES009605/R01 ES015572, NIOSH R01 OH007400 (publisher indexed acknowledgments)
financial_ties: Eskenazi disclosed consultation on pesticide exposure case; other authors declared no competing financial interests.
verification: Original PubMed abstract, grant and COI; indexed publisher funding
limitations: Residual confounding; nonspecific biomarkers; not personal prediction or evidence all produce unsafe.

title: Early childhood adversity potentiates the adverse association between prenatal organophosphate pesticide exposure and child IQ: the CHAMACOS cohort
quick: Family and environmental conditions can matter together.
details: Examines adversity as effect modifier of earlier CHAMACOS associations.
limitations: Same cohort P6-07, not independent replication.

title: Organic diets significantly lower children's dietary exposure to organophosphorus pesticides
quick: Switching to organic food reduced some pesticide biomarkers.
details: Urinary metabolites changed rapidly during dietary intervention.
limitations: Biomarker not clinical health benefit; no organic-only recommendation.

title: Effect of Organic Diet Intervention on Pesticide Exposures in Young Children Living in Low-Income Urban and Agricultural Communities
quick: Organic food lowered some but not all measured pesticide exposures.
details: Conventional 4 days, organic 7 days, conventional 5 days; several chemical-specific markers unchanged or infrequently detected.
limitations: Short-term urinary marker; no developmental outcomes or cost comparison.

title: The relationship between study sponsorship, risks of bias, and research outcomes in atrazine exposure studies conducted in non-human animals: Systematic review and meta-analysis
population: 51 studies; 39 at environmentally relevant concentrations as defined by reviewers
quick: Funding matters, but study design and results also matter.
details: Relevant subset: 11 industry,24 non-industry,4 no disclosure. No clear difference in assessed methodological risks; association with smaller harm effect sizes inconclusive.
financial_ties: Full reviewer disclosures and study-level sponsors not extracted
verification: Indexed primary PubMed/PMC/publisher results and funding
limitations: Animal studies only; no human prenatal risk estimate or named company share.

title: Birth weight and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid: a random-effects meta-regression analysis
quick: A company-funded review found lower birth weights overall but questioned whether PFOS caused the difference.
details: Overall -3.22 g per ng/mL; early -1.35, later -7.17; modeled intercept at start pregnancy +0.59, CI crosses zero.
financial_ties: All authors Ramboll employees compensated via employer; report no 3M role preparing manuscript, sole author control; no direct 3M compensation; not then testifying for sponsors about compound.
verification: Original PubMed abstract and conflict disclosure, figures 1–2 captions
limitations: Blood timing and plasma expansion/renal clearance confounding plausible; model intercept not directly observed effect; linear scale differs from P6-13; not evidence of fraud.

title: Birth weight in relation to maternal and neonatal biomarker concentration of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid: a meta-analysis and meta-regression from a systematic review
quick: EPA researchers found lower birth weights even in early-sampling studies.
details: Overall -30.3 g per natural-log unit PFOS; early -23.6 g. Timing did not explain all associations; funnel asymmetry p=.01.
funding: US EPA authored government work; grant statement not extracted separately
financial_ties: No competing interests declared; Dzierlenga also author of P6-12 with then-Ramboll affiliation. Prior dated employment not assumed current tie.
verification: Original PubMed abstract, affiliation, COI, figure 1/2 captions
limitations: Overlapping studies; units different from 2020 review, no direct numeric comparison; observational.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of birth weight and PFNA exposures
quick: Another PFAS was also linked with lower birth weight.
details: -32.9 g per natural-log ng/mL PFNA; sample timing did not fully explain association.
funding: EPA affiliations; full funding statement pending
limitations: Different compound, not add to PFOS or generalize to every PFAS.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of birth weight and prenatal exposure to perfluoroundecanoic acid
quick: New evidence suggests another PFAS may affect birth weight, but estimates remain uncertain.
details: Overall -15.3 g per ln ng/mL PFUnDA; early sample -6.8, interval crosses zero.
funding: EPA affiliations; full grant statement pending
financial_ties: No competing interests declared in PubMed
limitations: Different chemical; not safe threshold, no pooled group total.

title: Serum Vaccine Antibody Concentrations in Children Exposed to Perfluorinated Compounds
quick: PFAS exposure was associated with lower levels of some vaccine antibodies.
details: Example maternal PFOS doubling associated with -38.6% diphtheria antibody at age 5 prebooster (n510).
limitations: Antibody level is surrogate, not evidence vaccination ineffective; no change to immunization.

title: Guidance on PFAS Exposure, Testing, and Clinical Follow-Up
quick: Testing and follow-up are decisions to make with a clinician.
details: NASEM calls for more data on breastmilk/formula transfer and shared decisions.
limitations: Not an app blood test threshold or advice to stop breastfeeding.

title: Clinical Evaluation and Management: PFAS Information for Clinicians
quick: Reduce known sources; most nursing people should continue breastfeeding.
details: ATSDR has not set health-based blood-screening levels; contrasts NASEM recommendations. Tests do not predict specific future disease.
limitations: Clinical decisions; avoid universal biomonitoring and detox claims.

title: Reducing PFAS in Your Drinking Water with a Home Filter
quick: A certified filter may reduce PFAS, but not every filter works.
details: Activated carbon, ion exchange and RO options; certification scope and maintenance matter; EPA notes older standards not necessarily current MCL performance.
limitations: No specific product tested; check water results and certification.

title: Proposed PFOA and PFOS Compliance Extension Rule
quick: A proposed change to compliance dates is not a change in a chemical's health effects.
details: May 18 2026 proposal for eligible systems to request extension to 2031; separate proposed rescission of some other PFAS rules https://www.epa.gov/sdwa/proposed-pfas-rescission-rule.
limitations: Final legal status not comprehensively verified; do not hardcode deadlines or equate legal limit with safety.

title: Associations Between Prenatal Urinary Biomarkers of Phthalate Exposure and Preterm Birth: A Pooled Study of 16 US Cohorts
quick: Higher levels of some plastic-related chemicals were linked to slightly higher odds of early birth.
details: Four IQR increases: ORs 1.12,1.16,1.16,1.14; several intervals touch/cross null.
funding: NIH/NIEHS and EPA grants among disclosures; full grant list pending
financial_ties: McElrath disclosed NxPrenatal/Mirvie equity and advisory roles/fees from Roche, Momenta, Comanche, Tectonic; Braun plaintiffs' PFAS expert-witness work paid into institutional account, not salary; Cordero outside Medtronic Foundation grant. Relevant direct plastic-industry sponsor not established.
verification: Original JAMA disclosure and indexed primary abstract
limitations: Observational, correlated exposure; no individual risk forecast.

title: Periods of susceptibility for associations between phthalate exposure and preterm birth: Results from a pooled analysis of 16 US cohorts
quick: Timing might matter, but studies disagree on which trimester.
details: Uses earlier pooled cohort data; explicitly identifies overlap with ECHO (PROTECT,TIDES,Healthy Start,CCCEH,MARBLES).
financial_ties: Braun PFAS litigation disclosure noted in indexed full text; remaining disclosures pending
limitations: Not independent replication; no precise trimester-specific safe period.

title: Prenatal phthalate exposure and adverse birth outcomes in the USA: a prospective analysis of births and estimates of attributable burden and costs
population: 5006 mother-child dyads per linked cohort comparison
quick: Some replacement plasticizers were also linked to premature birth.
details: OR per log10 increase: DEHP 1.45; phthalic acid 2.71; DiNP 2.25; DiDP 1.69; DnOP 2.90.
verification: Indexed primary abstract and ECHO overlap from P6-22
limitations: Modeled attributable burden requires causality assumption; not verified preventable cases; overlap; no compare magnitude across different scaling.

title: Gestational Exposure to 10 Classes of Priority Chemicals and Birth Outcomes in the ECHO Cohort
quick: Newer data also link certain plasticizers with earlier birth.
details: Summed DiNP metabolites OR 1.16 for preterm birth; gestational age -0.6 days.
funding: Funding and COI not extracted from indexed results
limitations: ECHO overlap not yet mapped; no independent cohort count; multiple comparisons.

title: Food packaging and bisphenol A and bis(2-ethyhexyl) phthalate exposure: findings from a dietary intervention
population: Families, usual diet vs 3-day fresh food phase
quick: Less packaged food reduced some measured chemical exposures in this small study.
details: Urine geometric mean BPA -66%; DEHP metabolites -53 to -56%.
funding: Primary study grant statement not verified
financial_ties: Silent Spring Institute and Breast Cancer Fund author affiliations; not certified independent, advocacy context separate
limitations: Biomarkers, not pregnancy/child health outcomes; contrast P6-26.

title: Unexpected results in a randomized dietary trial to reduce phthalate and bisphenol A exposures
population: 10 families, 21 complete diet replacement vs19 written advice
quick: Even fresh-food interventions can unexpectedly increase exposure.
details: Median DEHP metabolites 283.7 to7027.5 nmol/g in supplied food arm; ingredient contamination, coriander and milk; written advice arm no clear change.
funding: University of Washington Center for Ecogenetics and Environmental Health, NIEHS ES007033 (indexed publisher acknowledgments)
limitations: Short study, particular ingredients; not evidence all spices or milk unsafe.

title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study
quick: Switching certain personal care products reduced some urinary chemicals.
details: MEP -27.4%; methyl paraben -43.9%; propyl paraben -45.4%; MnBP and MiBP no significant change.
funding: California Breast Cancer Research Program per state study page https://www.biomonitoring.ca.gov/projects/health-and-environmental-research-make-salinas-adolescents-hermosa-study
financial_ties: Full COI and product donations not extracted
verification: Indexed primary abstract, official project funding
limitations: Adolescent not pregnant/infant cohort; biomarker only; no automatic shopping list.

title: Large effects from small exposures. II. The importance of positive controls in low-dose research on bisphenol A
quick: An older review reported a striking difference in findings by funding.
details: 11/11 chemical-industry-funded studies reported no significant effect; 109 animal studies reported significant low-dose effects overall. No complete public-funded denominator extracted.
funding: PubMed tags NIH and non-US governmental support; exact grants pending
limitations: Historical, animal endpoints and narrative methods; no universal percentage, no direct human evidence, not current entire literature.

title: Re-evaluation of the risks to public health related to the presence of bisphenol A in foodstuffs
quick: European regulators assess BPA more cautiously than FDA.
details: EFSA 2023 TDI 0.2 ng/kg/day; immune evidence central; not a measured individual toxicity threshold.
financial_ties: Panel disclosures and review membership pending
limitations: Different methods/endpoints from FDA; not personal dose calculator.

title: Bisphenol A (BPA): Use in Food Contact Application
quick: FDA's published position differs from EFSA's.
details: FDA's assessment supports safety at current levels in foods; FDA reviews do not settle every endpoint or substitute chemical.
financial_ties: Panel and underlying study funding not audited
limitations: Agency disagreement not proof of corporate capture; verify current version before publication.

title: CLARITY-BPA Core Study: A Perinatal and Chronic Extended-Dose-Range Study of Bisphenol A in Rats
design: Regulatory animal experiment plus linked academic research
quick: Laboratory studies help investigate possible mechanisms but do not directly predict a baby's risk.
details: FDA guideline-compliant core study and NIEHS-funded academic studies share animal lineage.
limitations: Animal evidence; no human clinical inference; companion compendium https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK575830/.

title: Plasticenta: First evidence of microplastics in human placenta
quick: Tiny plastic particles were detected in some placental samples.
details: 12 fragments 5–10 micrometers in 4 of 6 placentas.
limitations: Very small sample; contamination and methods limitations; detection not clinical harm or prevalence.

title: Microplastic release from the degradation of polypropylene feeding bottles during infant formula preparation
quick: Heating and preparation can release plastic particles from some bottles.
details: Measured particle release, not infant absorption or health outcomes.
funding: Enterprise Ireland CF20180870; Science Foundation Ireland 12/RC/2278,16/IA/4462,16/RC/3889; Trinity engineering scholarship; China Scholarship Council awards
verification: Indexed original publisher abstract and grant statement; direct publisher blocked
limitations: Do not alter formula temperature/sterilization, concentration or storage; no clinical evidence glass improves health; avoid breakage.

title: Effects of Microplastic Exposure on Human Digestive, Reproductive, and Respiratory Health: A Rapid Systematic Review
design: Rapid systematic review integrating animal and human evidence
quick: Scientists suspect harms, but direct human evidence is limited.
details: Hazard assessment judged suspected harms; not dose-specific infant clinical risk.
funding: Full funding statement inaccessible in this pass
limitations: Human and animal evidence streams must remain distinct.

title: Health impacts of micro- and nanoplastics in humans: systematic review of in vivo evidence
design: Systematic review of human in vivo studies
quick: New human studies detect particles and possible links with health, but cannot yet tell us how much harm occurs.
details: Moderate-to-high confounding and exposure-measurement bias; no meta-analysis.
limitations: Search date discrepancy: abstract Dec 2024, Fig 1 caption Dec 2020; verify original methods before relying on coverage. Not evidence of causality.

title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Foods
quick: Current food measurements do not establish a human health risk at detected levels.
details: FDA position distinguishes detection from risk.
limitations: Not proof of safety at all exposures; reconcile with hazard reviews, no detox products.

title: Portable HEPA Filter Air Cleaner Use during Pregnancy and Children's Cognitive Performance at Four Years of Age: The UGAAR Randomized Controlled Trial
quick: Air filtration reduced particle exposure; a child cognition benefit was possible but uncertain.
details: 29% lower indoor PM2.5 in pregnancy; unadjusted IQ +2.5 points (CI -0.4 to5.4), adjusted for preterm imbalance +2.8 (-0.1 to5.7).
funding: Canadian Institutes of Health Research; Coway discounted modified cleaners
financial_ties: Complete author disclosures pending; not commercial-free due in-kind support
verification: Indexed original abstract, full-text funding/PM passage; PMC captcha
limitations: High pollution setting; not brand endorsement, interval crosses zero, attrition/imputation.

title: The effect of portable HEPA filter air cleaner use during pregnancy on fetal growth: The UGAAR randomized controlled trial
quick: Air cleaner evidence should be read across outcomes, not only the most favorable result.
details: Birth weight primary endpoint; exact estimate not extracted this pass.
funding: Same cohort funding P6-37; report-specific verification pending
limitations: Not independent replication; no birthweight effect claim until full extraction.

title: Liquefied Petroleum Gas or Biomass for Cooking and Effects on Birth Weight
population: 3200 pregnant participants, Guatemala, India, Peru, Rwanda
quick: Cleaner cooking reduced smoke exposure, but did not clearly improve birth weight.
details: Adjusted difference +19.6 g, CI -10.1 to49.2.
funding: NIH and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
verification: Indexed primary PubMed and NEJM HTML result
limitations: Biomass-to-LPG comparison in resource-limited settings, not US gas versus electric stove; no fuel recommendation.

title: Effects of Cooking with Liquefied Petroleum Gas or Biomass on Stunting in Infants
quick: The clean-cooking intervention also did not clearly prevent infant stunting.
details: Null primary stunting result per abstract; exact estimates pending.
funding: NIH and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
limitations: Same cohort; null not proof pollution harmless.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of heat exposure impacts on maternal, fetal and neonatal health
quick: Very hot weather is linked to more premature births.
details: Preterm odds OR 1.04 per 1°C increase (12 studies); heatwaves OR 1.26 (10 studies); stillbirth OR 1.13 CI crosses null.
limitations: Exposure metrics and baseline climates vary; not personal threshold; overlaps older heat reviews.

title: The influence of environmental exposures during the preconception period on offspring outcomes: a systematic review
population: 63 studies, maternal and paternal exposure before conception
quick: Both parents' workplace and environmental exposures deserve attention.
details: Search through May 2021; heterogeneous studies precluded meta-analysis.
verification: Original PubMed abstract, COI and registry
limitations: Sparse paternal data, older search, no quantified universal preconception period.

title: The influence of paternal preconception health on birth defects and head circumference: A scoping review
quick: Some workplace exposures in fathers have been linked to birth defects.
details: Reports associations with solvents, pesticides, metals and other paternal factors; primary effect extraction pending.
limitations: Cannot prove causality or promise prevention; primary study overlap with P6-42 pending.

title: Seminal and molecular evidence that sauna exposure affects human spermatogenesis
quick: Repeated high heat can temporarily change sperm measures.
details: Reported reversible impairment; no measured live birth or child health benefit of avoidance.
limitations: Small nonrandomized study; surrogate; no mandatory washout interval.

title: Heat exposure during susceptible windows of spermatogenesis and sperm epigenetic age
quick: Outdoor heat was linked with changes in sperm DNA methylation measures.
details: Sperm epigenetic age association, not child outcome.
funding: Parent trial NICHD intramural contracts HHSN275201200007C/HHSN275201300026I
limitations: No fertility or offspring causal inference; no automatic intervention.

title: Congenital anomalies in the offspring of occupationally exposed mothers: a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies using expert assessment for occupational exposures
quick: Solvents at work deserve a preconception and pregnancy safety review.
details: Associations with neural tube defects, congenital heart defects and orofacial clefts.
limitations: Occupational not household exposure; specific solvents and effect sizes pending.

title: Association of arsenic with adverse pregnancy outcomes/infant mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis
quick: Arsenic-contaminated water deserves testing and source control.
details: Birthweight association -53.2 g (-94.9 to -11.4) for review-defined exposure comparison; original unit/comparator unresolved.
limitations: Do not chart until scale and comparison verified; no universal risk from rice or water.

title: Association of arsenic exposure with adverse birth outcomes: A meta-analysis and a benchmark dose analysis
quick: Newer studies examine possible dose-response, but source control matters more than a modeled personal target.
details: Benchmark model with adverse pregnancy outcomes; exact estimates pending.
limitations: Model not individual threshold; check study overlap and exposure definition.
